rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50 (CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord or its agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental unit. Starting January 1, 2027, the cap is adjusted each year for CPI increases and published by the Division of Consumer Affairs.
rules.key_value: $50 max application fee, CPI-adjusted annually from 2027
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property offered for lease or sublease for dwelling purposes, other than units in one- or two-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent; New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees unless the licensee is the landlord of the property.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Real estate licensee exemption applies unless the licensee is the landlord.

rules.penalty: Up to $500 for a first offense, $750 for a second, and $1,000 for each subsequent offense, collected under the Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999. The wrongfully charged amount is refunded to the applicant from the penalty.
rules.quoted_span:
1. a. A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.conflict_note: The effective date is computed, not stated. The act takes effect on the first day of the fourth month next following enactment, and it was approved January 20, 2026, giving May 1, 2026. The min_units of 3 is inferred from the one- and two-family dwelling exemption.
